sections.h2: What should a Warren homeowner know before selling a house?
sections.html:
Selling in Warren comes down to three local pieces: a short list of city rules, the Macomb County Register of Deeds, and a tax calendar split between the city and the county. Warren is the largest community in Macomb County and the third-largest city in Michigan, so buyers, title companies and inspectors here handle these steps every week.

A cash buyer who takes the house as-is removes the showing and repair cycle. The deed still has to be recorded in Mount Clemens, the seller still owes the transfer tax, and any unpaid city bills still follow the parcel. The sections below cover those pieces in the order a seller meets them.

sections.h2: What is Warren like as a place to own a house?
sections.html:
Warren fills a square of about six miles by six miles in the southwest corner of Macomb County, running from 8 Mile Road in the south to 14 Mile Road in the north. It covers 34.4 square miles, shares its whole southern edge with Detroit, and wraps around the small city of Center Line. The first settlement, Beebe's Corners, started in 1830 at Mound Road and Chicago Road, and Warren became a city on January 1, 1957.

The housing stock reflects that history. Population jumped from 42,653 in 1950 to 179,260 in 1970, driven by the Detroit Arsenal Tank Plant, the Chrysler truck plant and the General Motors Technical Center. In Southeast Warren, much of the housing is the bungalow style built right after World War II. North of Stephens Road, many homes date from after 1960 and follow the brick ranch pattern.

  • Southeast Warren includes Warrendale, Belangers Garden, Berkshire Manor and Piper Van Dyke.
  • Southwest Warren includes the Fitzgerald and Beierman Farms neighborhoods.
  • Northeast Warren includes Bear Creek, Bella Vista Estates, Fairlane Estates and the downtown area.
  • Northwest Warren is centered on the western half of the Warren Con neighborhood.

Winters are a real factor for an older house here. Warren stays below freezing all day on about 39 days a year, so the furnace, roof and plumbing are the first things a buyer's inspector checks.

sections.h2: Who employs Warren residents, and how do the roads connect them?
sections.html:
The city's 2022 financial report lists General Motors as the largest employer, with 23,823 employees. The federal government follows at 7,800 (the Detroit Arsenal and its Army command), then Stellantis at 5,523, Ascension Health at 2,407 and Lipari Foods at 1,300. That concentration of steady employers is why Warren buyers often include people relocating within a short drive.

I-696 crosses the city east to west. M-53 (Van Dyke Avenue) splits it north to south, M-97 (Groesbeck Highway) cuts diagonally through the southeast, and Mound Road is the other main north-south artery. SMART provides bus service. The Census Bureau reports a mean commute of 24.9 minutes for Warren workers.

Six public school districts serve Warren, overseen by the Macomb Intermediate School District, and Macomb Community College has a campus in the city. Because district lines cut through the city, a buyer will want to confirm the district for a specific address before relying on a school name.

sections.h2: What do the Census figures say about Warren housing?
sections.html:
The Census Bureau estimated 137,138 residents for July 1, 2025, down 1.6 percent from the April 2020 base. For 2020 through 2024 it counts 54,744 households averaging 2.50 people, with 71.1 percent of homes owner-occupied.

The median value of an owner-occupied Warren home is $193,400, median gross rent is $1,225 a month, and median household income is $64,016. Median monthly owner costs run $1,403 with a mortgage and $557 without one. These are citywide medians, so a specific house can sit well above or below them.

sections.h2: Which Warren city rules affect a sale?
sections.html:
Warren's residential city certification, as the posted application describes it, covers a vacant dwelling that has been posted "no occupancy": nobody may move in until the Building Division confirms the house meets the International Property Maintenance Code and the zoning ordinance. The Building Division is at One City Square, Suite 305, phone 586-574-4504.

Rental owners face more. The rental ordinance posted by the Rental Inspections Division sets these terms:

  • No one may rent or occupy a rental dwelling without a rental license, and licenses do not transfer between landlords or units.
  • A license lasts two years and needs a biennial inspection.
  • Sale of the property ends the license immediately.
  • No license is issued until prior property taxes, special assessments, water or sewer bills and mowing or cleanup charges are paid.

A landlord selling a tenant-occupied house should ask the Rental Inspections Division (586-574-4633) where the license stands before listing, because open balances show up in the same way a tax lien does.

sections.h2: Where is a Warren deed recorded, and what does it cost?
sections.html:
Warren is in Macomb County, so deeds go to the Macomb County Register of Deeds at 120 N. Main St., Mount Clemens, open Monday through Friday from 8 a.m. to 4:15 p.m., phone 586-469-7953. Since October 1, 2016 the office has charged a flat fee per document regardless of page count.

Macomb County recording charges. Source: Macomb County Register of Deeds recording fee and transfer tax pages.
ItemCharge
Deed, mortgage or other instrument$30 per document
Document assigning or discharging several instruments$3 added for each extra instrument
Tax certificate (warranty deeds, land contracts)$5 for up to five legal descriptions
State transfer taxSale price multiplied by .0075
Macomb County transfer taxSale price multiplied by .0011

A warranty deed or land contract needs the county treasurer's tax certificate before it can be recorded. Michigan puts the transfer tax on the seller, and the county's schedule lists it in $500 steps if you want to look up an exact amount.

sections.h2: When are Warren property taxes due?
sections.html:
Warren bills summer taxes (city and school) in the first week of July and winter taxes (county) in the first week of December. The city treasurer's page sets the following schedule, and the Treasurer's Office at 586-574-4542 can confirm the current year's dates.

  • Summer tax can be paid in full, or in two installments if the first is paid by August 31. The second installment is billed December 1 and due by January 31.
  • After August 31 only the full summer balance is accepted, with a 1 percent collection fee in September and half a percent each month after.
  • Winter tax is payable from December 1 through February 28.
  • Anything unpaid after February 28 moves to the Macomb County Treasurer, with an added 4 percent fee and 1 percent interest per month.

Ask the title company how the current bills will be split at closing. A missed bill can hold up a rental license or a clean title, so check the balance with the Treasurer's Office before accepting an offer.

faqs.q: Do I need a city inspection to sell my Warren house?
faqs.a: The city certification on Warren's posted application covers vacant houses marked no occupancy, which must pass a Building Division inspection before anyone moves in. Call 586-574-4504 to ask whether your parcel carries that posting.

faqs.q: What happens to a Warren rental license when I sell the property?
faqs.a: It ends right away. The rental ordinance says sale of the property terminates the license, and licenses cannot be transferred. The buyer applies for a new one and the unit goes through a fresh inspection.

faqs.q: Who pays the transfer tax on a Warren sale?
faqs.a: The seller pays. Macomb County prints the state rate as sale price times .0075 and the county rate as sale price times .0011, and the amount is collected when the deed is recorded in Mount Clemens.

faqs.q: Where do I record a deed for a house in Warren?
faqs.a: Record it with the Macomb County Register of Deeds, 120 N. Main St., Mount Clemens. The office charges $30 per document, and a warranty deed also needs a tax certificate from the county treasurer.

faqs.q: What if I fall behind on Warren property taxes before selling?
faqs.a: Pay the Warren Treasurer's Office by February 28 on the winter bill. After that date the balance goes to the Macomb County Treasurer with extra fees and monthly interest, so clear the bill first or ask the title company to include it in the payoff.
